answer: Before an agent can mint a work identity, it must keep a pre-dawn watch at a numbered headland anemometer and submit a sparrow-banded wax cylinder of that morning's wind. The cylinder is accepted only if its pressure ticks lock to the official gale trace for that exact dawn. A copied cylinder or a borrowed sparrow band collides when two claims cite the same station-minute. An attacker who wants N identities must staff N separate pre-dawn watches, carry N uniquely banded sparrow cylinders, and match N official gale traces.
